title: MongoDB, DynamoDB, Cassandra, Neo4j and InfluxDB

videos.script: Five databases, one at a time, each started, asked two questions and removed. {{plan}} MongoDB holds a show as one document. Without an index it reads all hundred to find thirty four; with one, it reads thirty four. Renaming a venue rewrites thirty three documents. {{mongo}} DynamoDB finds one buyer's tickets in one partition, and refuses a question that does not name the buyer. A scan reads everything, and that is what you pay for. {{dynamo}} Cassandra returns the latest scans of a show already sorted, and refuses to filter by gate unless you insist. It used eight hundred megabytes for six rows. {{cassandra}} Neo4j walks from a show to its buyers to their other shows, touching only the paths. {{neo4j}} InfluxDB sums three hours of sales by the hour, and forgets them after thirty days on its own. {{influx}}
